title: Question before buying and launching my project

posts.author: Jeenah
posts.body:
Hello there ! As you can probably see, i'm a total newbie on this forum and community despite my long-time interest for it.
I'm actually thinking about creating an RPG with RPG Maker (MZ Seems to be the best for what i envision).
I have a good idea of what i want for this game :
- Open World / World Map for fast travel => (Basically, the possibility to travel the entire world by navigating the maps like a Skyrim [Going from instance to instance, the entire world would be perfectly connected together] => And possibility for the player to litteraly die to an ennemy that would be too strong for them (Or gain valuable items for defeating said very strong ennemy).
- Farming elements (Especially at the start of the game + crafting like a stardew valley) => And gain XP from said crafting and farming [Not a lot, but still some XP]
=> Player need to be able to harvest or even plant some medicinal plants to craft potions with the proper ingredients (Lore accurate since the main character of the game would be a jack of all trades [Not voluntarily])
- Adjusted stats and stat growth. I intend to make the game kind of realistic in terms of Health values and keep it small in numbers. (The main character, which will start as a child would not have more than 20 HP and like 5 or 6 mana at best).
His starting companion would have just 10 (Bird of prey/eagle).
- Are there resources for a hawk/bird of prey (Party member), big red dragon (party member AND ennemy), black wolf/demon black wolf (Party member AND ennemy) ?
=> Will need a lot more probably but they're the most important for this story. They're crucial, even. Without them, no story at all.
As to why i would need that. The main character would be like a Beast Charmer/Tamer but i'm more inclined to say charmer. Those beasts would not be under his control, but would still be "chill" towards his existence. (Like a pacifier for wild beasts/monsters).
I hope my explanations arn't too confusing, english isn't my main langage. (Thanks to correct if you see any gramatical or weird use of words).
- Game would need some very special events / dialogues in combat.
- Timed event on world map or normal maps (Optional, but would still be cool if possible).
- Beautiful and lively maps. The game would be better appreciated by traveling the entire world on foot instead of fast-traveling with big emphasis on exploration since that would be part of the main goal/quest of the main character [IMPORTANT]
So is all of this available or even possible ? Thank you in advance, i don't want to get my hopes up and them have them crushed while developping the game midway. (Most horrible feeling i had multiple times).
I have some experience as a kitbasher for ships on the game Starsector, some in coding but i don't think its much.

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body:
While technically all of this is certainly possible, it would take an incredible amount of effort to make an open world game with so many features for just one person, especially one who's new to it. I don't know how much content and of what quality do you expect to include, but this sounds a lot more like a decade-long project than something that can be done in a year.
I'd recommend doing some
much
smaller projects (e.g. participating in one week-long game jams) to get a better feel for the engine and what exactly can you do with it.
And the obligatory reminder that the first game you'll ever make will most likely be rather terrible, because you have no experience making games yet. Make smaller ones, learn from them, and slowly progress to larger and larger projects until you're confident that you can actually finish your dream game.

posts.author: Arcaines
posts.body:
Welcome tot he forums! So, first, yes, all of this is possible in RPG maker. It's just a matter of finding the plugins for them.
2nd, IF this is your first RPG Maker project, appealing as open world maybe I wouldn't recommend doing one on your own unless the scale of said open world is small, otherwise you may get burnt out due to the sheer amount of needed to put into a open world. But that's my advice and should be taken as a must. If you want to make a open, go ahead.
You could, however, start a prototype, get some work done on it and try recruiting some people to join and help.

The biggest limitation would be the required content.
a large world map needs a lot of content (and no, random encounters are not content) or the player gets bored when traveling through it.
But each place you have on the world map will take you dozens of hours to create.
as said above it is a question of scale, and you need experience to be able to handle large scales.
Other than that there are technical limitations (both to size and number of maps), but those are big enough that they shouldn't pose problems - like the maps max being 250x250 while most world maps bein between 80x80 and 150x150.

You didnt mention how you were doing encounters. Id suggest against that if you're doing random encounters and escape isn't guaranteed.
When you get your arms torn off by a Territorial Rotbart, deathclaw, or whatever have you, some of the fault is on you as the player. you can see them from a distance. If they snuck up on you, you weren't paying attention.
If a player takes a step they had to take towards a goal and the game randomly decides that theyre suddenly fighting something they have no means of beating at their level, that's just a loss that they could not prevent.
If you say something like "stick to the roads. Dangerous beasts avoid them." and have paths that connect locations where you cant encounter the local noob annihilator, that's one thing. But if every tile on the way somewhere has a chance of just causing a game over, Id wager more people would find it frustrating than not

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Having an ultimate goal for a game in mind is fine, but I recommend putting it on the back burner for a while as a new user first learning MZ.
Everything you want to do is doable. But it would probably be better to focus first on watching/reading tutorials and recreating them. If you can’t follow the built in tutorial, then I fear that most of what you want to do will be extremely challenging.
After you have done some tutorials and explored the built in Event Commands, I would start experimenting on pieces of what you ultimately want to do. By experimenting, you will learn a LOT.
Being a solo dev is slow work and you really need to take the time to learn the basics. And as you get more experienced, what you want to do will get easier and easier. And you will learn better ways to do things.
And you can find a lot of help here on the forum and plenty of free resources too.
Welcome to the forum and good luck on your projects!

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
Learning how to modify resources is all well and good (and where I started my RPG Maker career, so I'd be a hypocrite of the highest degree of I said otherwise XD) but there's only so much you can learn from a tutorial without the actual software in front of you. I'd really recommend that you experiment with what's provided before you leap into changing it.
Making rounded cave tiles before you've ever tried mapping a cave is a bit like trying to furnish a house before you've built the walls! And you may find that those "imperfect pixels" were deliberately placed to help anchor the bridges into their surroundings. Making tilesets is arguably my favorite part of making games, but it's really important to try what's provided to make sure you understand how they work. It'll save you so much frustration later!
